reviews.title: Good flights between Kathmandu and Pokhara
reviews.text: The road from Kathmandu to Pokhara is often blocked by landslides and rockfalls during the monsoon season and in 2022 has been blocked several times. The quickest way to get to Pokhara is a 23 minute flight – much better than the 7 or 8 hour drive. All airlines in Nepal charge foreigners a higher fare than the locals and even if you are the only foreigner on a plane, you are paying over US$20 extra than all those sitting around you. Buddha Air is the biggest domestic service and I found them to be very well organised and both flights were good. Basically you take off, climb for about 5 minutes, level out for 5 minutes then descend and land. Buddha Air has built a new domestic terminal at Kathmandu airport which is clean with plenty of seating. You are then taken on a bus out to the plane and off you go. The plane was clean – an ATR72 twin engine turboprop short haul plane developed and produce in France and Italy which can carry between 72 and 78 passengers. Pokhara is a delight to land at – clean, spacious, surrounded by huge mountains with the beautiful Phewa Tal Lake in the centre, but very humid and hot during the monsoon. Can highly recommend Buddha Air – they seem to be well organised and both flights were good.

reviews.title: Mountain Flight aka Everest Experience
reviews.text: Booked direct online to do the scenic flight passing the Himalayas and Mount Everest. About 8 Buddha Air flights were all scheduled at the exact same time (6:30am) so don’t expect to depart on time. Nor should your flight number be an indication of in which order you will depart. I was flight 101. The other flights were 100, 102, 103, 104, 200, 400, 600. Flight 103 went first. Then 400. There was no logic. I didn’t care, it’s Nepal, they do things their way! The main thing was we eventually left and had perfect skies and a great co pilot who took photos for us. We had seatbelts. Seats about 18 passengers. The small plane had only window seats someberyone gets a view. Windows oval shaped and row 7 has the wing obstructing view a little. Some little scratches,on the window as you would expect for old planes. Some condensation gathers as it goes up into the cold atmosphere. Pilot’s window provide great photos. Left side see the mountains first. We could visit the front to look out the clear cockpit windows lots of times. The weather was hazy on the ground (extreme pollution) but above the brown layer it was a perfect layer. You get a little mountain map and a certificate at the end. Well worth the money. Highly recommend it. (Did not fly to Pokhara, just had to enter a destination to submit this review)

reviews.title: Smooth Flying - Pokhara to Chitwan
reviews.text: We actually had several flights with Buddha Air, the Pokhara to Chitwan being just one of them. All flights were smooth and for the most part on time. The usual reason for delays in Nepal is the weather and I'd rather have a delayed flight and be safe. The staff were great and we had no problems getting updated information. Some of the flights were on quite small planes, but I love flying and am not bothered about the size of the plane. Thanks for getting us around your beautiful country safely, Buddha Air!

reviews.title: Flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara
reviews.text: I travelled from Kathmandu to Pokhara by Buddha Air last month. The flight was only for 25 minutes. Flight delays are normal in Nepal, it was 2 hours delay due to bad weather. Please make sure to come to airports well in advance, especially for international flights, because security checks take a lot of time.

reviews.author: 187147George

reviews.title: Local flight in Nepal
reviews.text: The flight is only for 25 minutes, but it is a flight nevertheless, and at first I was concerned about its safety. It was quite unusual to fly not in a jet airplane, but the experience turned out to be great. The local airport was another story. It was quite hectic with lots of people looking for information on their flights, many of which were delayed. But flight delays are normal in Nepal, just do not fret over it since you cannot change anything, anyway. Rather than waiting for my flight appear on the Departures screen, I showed my boarding pass to an employee and got all the info I needed. When travelling in Nepal, never panic. There is always someone around who speaks English. Make sure to come to airports well in advance, especially for international flights, because security checks take a lot of time. Keep your bagage sticker, you will need to present kt when getting your suitcase upon arrival.
reviews.author: IrinaYasinova

reviews.title: Budget travel
reviews.text: If you want to travel between Kathmandu and Kolkata, Buddha Air is one of the best. The money charged is practically within your budget and you get a cordial and comfortable service. You also get food during your trip. The timings are perfect. Overall a good option.

reviews.title: Pathetic experience with Buddha Air
reviews.text: Buddha Air has been running flights internationally since two months and still they cant provide any automated boarding pass, it was provided to us manually and we have to wait for around 40 mins after immigration as they are going to get a letter in hand for our security check-in!! Then the pathetic situation arrived when we were announced that the flight cant land in kathmandu airas it was shut down due to an emergency and so we will be shifted to Bhadrapur Airport which is nearby.Apart from the recurrent turbulence which we faced while flying, we were just locked in a waiting room for 6 hours as we are international passengers and we cant leave the port without immigration. So our boarding pass and main luggage was also ceased by the authorities. After shouting we were shifted to a nearby hotel which was horrible, beyond mh imagination that internationally flying passengers can ever be kept in such hotels!! But in vain, no use repeatedly complaining to them. In the early morning we were informed that airbus will come to pick up at 5.30 as our flight was scheduled for 7.00,but as usual it was delayed without any sort of providing us any information. It was a hell experience with Buddha Air. They dont have the capability of running international flights and aren't aware or rather bothered about knowing the terms and conditions in such emergency circumstances.
reviews.author: SPB

reviews.title: Flight is always delayed
reviews.text: I use Buddha air for domestic flights and have frequently flown to Dhangadi,Pokhara, Nepalgunj,Bhairahawa ,Bharatpur, Simara, Janakpur and Bhadrapur Airport.The flight is usually delayed. Always expect a 45 minutes to 1 hour delay on every flight. On summer, the cabin temperature is a little high despite AC working inside,so you might get some sweat. Since it's a turbo prop and flies relatively lower than jets,be ready for little shake especially on cloudy weather due to turbulence.It's the most used Domestic carrier of Nepal specially with sound safety record & Other services are good.
reviews.author: Swaviman Acharya

reviews.title: Recommend flying with them
reviews.text: When we arrived at Kathmandu domestic terminal there was chaos as the runway had not yet been opened to flights after overnight maintenance. The domestic terminal was packed but the Buddha Air ground staff were helpful as they kept us up to date about when the flight might leave - it was an hour and a half late. I had assumed we would be flying to Pokhara on one the bigger ATR planes and my face went pale as we pulled up beside a tiny Beechcraft plane which takes just 19 people. We took off in this tiny plane surrounded by the big international jets and in just 24 minutes had climbed, levelled off and then descended and landed in Pokhara - a very smooth flight. After the stay in Pokhara we did fly back to Kathmandu in one of the bigger ATRs which was very comfortable - so I'd say for a domestic service both flights were very professional.

reviews.title: You are lucky if it is on time

reviews.author: amars777

reviews.title: Great service, especially when flight was running late
reviews.text: Buddha Airlines is a Nepalese regional carrier. Their fleet seem to primarily comprise of turboprop planes that serve Nepal and adjoining countries. We took Buddha Air roundtrip from Kathmandu to Bhairawa. The plane was an ATR turboprop commuter planes - it was clean and comfortable enough for the short flight. The flight attendants were gracious and helpful. Given the short flight, cabin service was limited to peanuts and a drink. Both flights suffered from flight delays in excess of an hour. I am not sure what caused the delays. On the flight back to Kathmandu, we were likely to miss our connection on our outbound international flight. We spoke with the flight attendant about our situation and she spoke with the Captain and Operations. When we landed in Kathmandu, they pulled our luggage aside and ordered a van to come to the plane and ferry us to the domestic airport exit. The international terminal is a short walk from the domestic terminal. We barely made our connection; however, we wouldn't have made it if Buddha Air hadn't pulled out the stops to help us reduce the time at baggage claim and transit to the terminal. If I'm in Nepal again, I will certainly give Buddha another go.
